decisions.reason: The splash target and conditional guard policy do not change the bowl removal or rapid-swapping behavior. The separate cleaning clause already has its own same-message MODIFY.
Splash containment does not alter the required mixing texture or foam quality. The source message's strong-and-frothy target is already represented by a separate same-message MODIFY.

The candidate's same-message MODIFY already captures the independently stated solenoid, flow, and operation-sequence decisions. The splash target and optional bowl guard require no additional dispensing-state change.
An optional splash guard or lip does not change the selected bowl capacity, depth, or size reference.
The splash-control modification does not change the spout's location, orientation, construction, or appearance.
The splash target and conditional guard policy do not alter either specified color.
Splash containment does not change the machine name, retained wording, or customer-facing placard placement.
The optional use of a splash guard does not replace or modify the DJ-turntable-inspired visual identity.
The product-level splash requirement does not change the candidate's general layout deliverable or adopted design direction.
The conditional splash-guard policy does not necessarily change the current V1 priority or sourcing policy.
The source reiterates good sealing and prevention of leaks into the base, but those constraints already exist in the candidate state and no value or scope change is established.

The splash target and optional guard do not change whisk size, bowl compatibility, mixing medium, or whisk style. The source's separate whisk-material question does not establish a confirmed replacement.
